Reddit: risotto.nav: Skip to main content Open menu Open navigation Go to Reddit Home Get App Log In Expand user menu Home Popular Answers Explore All Communities Resources About Reddit Advertise Help Blog Careers Press
Reddit: risotto.article: r/Cooking • 5 hr. ago Why does my risotto turn out gluey instead of creamy? I use arborio rice, toast it in butter, add white wine, then hot stock one ladle at a time while stirring. After 18 minutes it's thick and gluey. What am I doing wrong? Upvote 342 Downvote 87 Go to comments Share Sort by: Best You're probably overcooking it. Take it off when the rice is still al dente and finish with butter and parmesan off the heat. Reply Award Share Keep the stock at a simmer and don't stir constantly, just often. Carnaroli rice is more forgiving than arborio. Reply Award Share Loose and wavy is what you want, all'onda. It thickens as it sits on the plate. Reply Award Share

Reddit: async JavaScript.article: r/javascript • 5 hr. ago async/await vs promise chains in Node.js: which do you use? Our codebase mixes .then() chains and async functions. Is there any performance difference, and how do you handle errors with Promise.all inside async functions? Upvote 342 Downvote 87 Go to comments Share Sort by: Best No real performance difference, async/await is syntax over promises. Use try/catch around await. Reply Award Share Promise.all rejects on the first error; use Promise.allSettled if you need every result. Reply Award Share Remember the event loop: await yields, so long synchronous loops still block Node. Reply Award Share
